pressures.name: Anthrax outbreak in DR Congo wildlife
Fake nuclear alerts via hacked apps
Oleshky ceasefire collapse and Kherson evacuations

chair.lede: Four new pressures emerge, pushing the clock down by 1.0 second overall.
body: Severe flash flooding in the U.S. Southwest and a second cyclone threatening India illustrate a sharp rise in climate‑related disasters, warranting a modest pressure addition.
An anthrax outbreak that killed hippos in the Virunga National Park highlights a new zoonotic risk amplified by drought and conflict.
Cyber‑enabled disinformation campaigns sent fake nuclear and chemical alerts to emergency apps in Ukraine and Russia, raising panic and safety concerns.
The expiration of the Oleshky ceasefire and renewed civilian evacuations in Kherson signal a deterioration in the Ukraine conflict.

experts.say: No new nuclear weapon test, treaty change, or substantive escalation appears; the reports are about drills, talks, and cyber‑alert hoaxes, which do not add a fresh danger beyond existing pressures.

Severe flash flooding in the Southwest and Colorado and a second Indian cyclone this week highlight escalating extreme weather, while drought‑linked anthrax deaths in Congo’s Virunga park (10) show climate stress on ecosystems. The shift of US Democrats away from climate policy (18) adds political risk.
Anthrax outbreak kills hippos in DR Congo’s Virunga National Park, highlighting a new zoonotic disease event that could spill over to humans amid drought and conflict.

Recent cyberattacks spoofed emergency alert apps in Ukraine and Russia, spreading fake nuclear and radiation warnings. This new misuse of AI‑enabled disinformation heightens the risk of panic and undermines critical infrastructure safety.
The expiration of the Oleshky ceasefire and renewed evacuations in Kherson signal a worsening of the Ukraine conflict (41).
